generatedCommentsNodes.comment: The comment above `getTruncatedInput()` suggests using an object with a single field for `TRUNCATED_RECORD_KEY`. However, the implementation uses an anonymous class with overridden methods. Consider creating a dedicated class or static factory method to improve clarity and maintainability.

The `getTruncatedInput()` and `getTruncatedWatchExecutionResult()` methods create new instances of `ExecutableInput` and `WatchExecutionResult` respectively, which are not thread-safe if shared across threads. Ensure that these methods are called in a context where the returned objects are not shared between threads.

The test case `testPutLargeHistory` checks for the presence of `TRUNCATED_RECORD_KEY` in the source map, but it does not verify that other fields are indeed missing or truncated as expected. Enhance the test to ensure comprehensive coverage of the truncation logic.

The test cases in `HistoryIntegrationTests` and the logic in `HistoryStore#put` assume that the size of the serialized JSON is directly comparable to the `maxHistoryRecordSize`. This might not be accurate if there are differences in encoding or additional metadata added during serialization. Consider using a more robust method to estimate the size of the serialized data.

review_comment: I'm also assuming that adding a new field to the history store doesn't need any further changes to mappings or anything?

It looks like `input` doesn't specify dynamic, so it defaults to dynamic (https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/main/x-pack/plugin/core/template-resources/src/main/resources/watch-history.json#L108). And `result` is explicitly dynamic (https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/main/x-pack/plugin/core/template-resources/src/main/resources/watch-history.json#L136).
